predicate.criterion: The cancel_pending_order 'reason' argument (one of 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake') must match what the user actually said about why they want to cancel -- not a value the agent picked/defaulted without the user ever stating or agreeing to that specific reason. Because the reason is a fixed two-value enum, near-paraphrase is acceptable when the user's statement clearly and uniquely favors one of the two values under ordinary-language interpretation (e.g. 'I don't want it anymore' -> 'no longer needed'), even if not verbatim. It is still a FAIL if the agent's chosen reason has no reasonable textual support in what the user said, or if the user's stated reason is genuinely compatible with both fixed values and the agent picked one without asking a clarifying question.

declined_without_attempting_alternative.criterion: This is judging a real retail delivered-order item-exchange conversation (retail_078_state#b0, docs/agentcoveragetesting_reuse_log.md section 186). This requirement_text/tool_call_error_matches check is used by this ONE branch, whose real Given is that the specific item_id the user asks to exchange does not actually exist in this delivered order at all, so the real exchange_delivered_order_items tool would raise 'Number of <item_id> not found.'. The assistant is NOT required to have attempted the exchange_delivered_order_items call at all. Based only on the real transcript, determine whether the assistant correctly declined to exchange that item, and whether its stated reason is genuinely grounded in real information actually available in this conversation (e.g. a real get_order_details result whose real item list does not contain the requested item_id) -- not a fabricated reason, and not a refusal for some other, unrelated cause (e.g. wrong order ownership, or an order status the transcript does not show) that never actually engages the item's real absence from the order. Asking the user to clarify which item they meant, based on the order's real item list, counts as correctly engaging the constraint. A refusal that never engages this real constraint at all, or that misstates what the transcript actually shows, is a FAIL.

Based only on the real transcript, determine whether the assistant correctly declined the user's request to modify this order's items, and whether its stated reason is genuinely grounded in real information actually available in this conversation (e.g. a real get_order_details result correctly showing either the item's real absence from the order, or the order's real 'pending (item modified)' status) -- matching the ONE real reason this conversation's own transcript actually establishes, not a fabricated or unrelated reason, and not a refusal for some other, unrelated cause (e.g. wrong order ownership) that never actually engages either real constraint. summary.retraction_reason: docs/agentcoveragetesting_reuse_log.md section 183: the frozen upstream Then grants a permission ('may modify / may exchange / may return ...') that the branch's own Given status rules out -- tau2 retail tools.py rejects the call for that status ('Non-pending order cannot be modified', 'Non-delivered order cannot be exchanged/returned') and policy.md's tool-specific rule forbids it. An upstream Step1-2 spec-authoring defect (per-tool instantiation of the generic 'take action on pending or delivered orders' rule), not a compiler or binder bug; each had zero executable checks. Each is replaced, in the same position, by its corrected prohibition sibling from the retail_session183_standalone extension release (retail_067_state_*#e1, exchange #e3), same Given/When, Then 'The agent must not ...'.
